Description: Neutral grip pressing is well tolerated by the right shoulder
SupportingEvidence: Consistent across floor press, DB neutral press, and machine press across all phases
Notes: Fundamental finding that guides all pressing selection

Description: Right anterior shoulder capsule awareness occurs during heavy pressing, especially floor press and machine press eccentric phase
SupportingEvidence: Noted in every phase during pressing; more prominent at heavier weights and during eccentric phase
Notes: Not pain but consistent tightness/awareness; worsens with fatigue

Description: Overhead pressing tolerance has progressively improved across phases
SupportingEvidence: Phase 3: cautious introduction; Phase 6: inverted KB holds; Phase 8: seated neutral grip DB OHP at 50 lbs
Notes: Progressed from zero overhead work to loaded overhead pressing

Description: Slight lean-back on cable pulldowns eliminates right anterior capsule awareness
SupportingEvidence: Consistent finding on single arm neutral grip cable pulldowns across Phases 5-8
Notes: 10-15 degrees of lean back resolves the issue

Description: Overhead cable extensions seem to loosen the anterior capsule after chest pressing
SupportingEvidence: Noted in Phase 6 and Phase 7 that capsule feels better after overhead tricep work
Notes: May be a useful exercise sequencing insight

Description: Grip endurance remains a limiting factor on carries, rows, and RDLs
SupportingEvidence: Grip failure occurs before target muscle failure on farmer's walks, chest supported rows, and DB RDLs consistently
Notes: Primary training limitation alongside shoulder

Description: Right grip tends to fail before left on farmer's walks and RDLs
SupportingEvidence: Right index finger rolls first; left pinky rolls first; different failure patterns
Notes: Asymmetric grip failure pattern

Description: Forearm lactic acid buildup precedes finger roll during grip failure
SupportingEvidence: Burning sensation in forearms consistently precedes weight rolling to fingertips
Notes: Suggests forearm endurance is the root cause rather than finger strength

Description: Left bicep contraction is slightly weaker than right, especially under fatigue
SupportingEvidence: Left contraction fails first on curls; left squeeze less forceful; left resists supination more
Notes: Consistent across all curl variations

Description: Left trap tends to engage compensatorily during lateral raises, pressing, and overhead movements
SupportingEvidence: Left trap shrugging noted during lateral raises, DB press, and overhead press; self-corrected when noticed
Notes: Likely compensation pattern

Description: Strict tempo enforcement produces better muscle connection than heavier weight with loose tempo
SupportingEvidence: Phase 6 spider curls at lower weight with strict 2-1-3 tempo produced better pump than heavier sets with loose tempo
Notes: Led to tempo re-emphasis in Phase 8

Description: Training on a significant caloric deficit severely impairs performance
SupportingEvidence: Phase 5 Day 1 session with significant caloric deficit resulted in near-illness, carry failure, and early termination
Notes: Single event but dramatic enough to validate

Description: Body row grip slips from sweat accumulation during high-volume sessions
SupportingEvidence: Grip slipping on barbell during body rows when hands are sweaty from prior exercises
Notes: Addressed with paper towels; not a structural limitation

Description: Planet Fitness cable machines may use approximately half the plate weight displayed
SupportingEvidence: Kneeling single arm rope extension: plate reads 40 but feels like 20 lbs; pattern noted across multiple exercises
Notes: Needs systematic verification; affects all PF cable weight logging

Description: Cable external rotation: left has less ROM than right
SupportingEvidence: Noted during cable external rotation warmup in Phase 3
Notes: May be related to overall left-side compensation patterns

Description: Nausea occurs during high-intensity compound movements, especially goblet squats and rowing finishers
SupportingEvidence: Phase 8 Day 3: nausea after goblet squat set 3; diarrhea after rowing finisher
Notes: Sneeze/puke sensation described; resolves with short rest

Description: Radial tilt on floor press reduces right anterior capsule awareness
SupportingEvidence: Shifting to slight radial tilt during neutral grip floor press felt better on capsule
Notes: Fine-tuning of pressing grip angle

Description: Superior humeral glide observed during single arm cable extensions; anchoring down resolves it
SupportingEvidence: Noted during Phase 6 single arm cable extensions
Notes: Corrected by consciously depressing humeral head

Description: Plate pinch grip: left hand tends to slip before right
SupportingEvidence: During plate pinch holds at 50 lbs, left hand consistently loses grip first
Notes: Opposite pattern from farmer's walk (right fails first)

Description: Single arm overhead cable extension: left arm fatigues faster than right
SupportingEvidence: Left side consistently reaches failure 2-4 reps before right on overhead cable extensions
Notes: Matches left bicep weakness pattern; suggests left arm is generally weaker

Description: Cable fly ROM should be slightly shortened to manage right anterior capsule awareness
SupportingEvidence: Full cable fly extension triggers right anterior tightness; shortened ROM eliminates it
Notes: Effective self-management strategy

Description: High cable tricep pushdown: shoulders roll forward if ROM exceeds 90-100 degrees
SupportingEvidence: ROM creeping above 90-100 degrees causes shoulder roll-forward compensation
Notes: Keeping strict 90-100 degree ROM maintains proper form
